beats.text: Before a speed-dating event, people listed what they wanted in a partner.
Men said looks mattered more to them. Women said earning potential.
But at the actual dates, those things mattered about the same for men and women.
What people said they wanted had little to do with who they actually liked.
So maybe your type is just a theory. Go on the date anyway.

sources: Eastwick & Finkel (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: Do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 94(2). Stated sex-differentiated preferences (looks, earning prospects) did not predict actual attraction at speed dating; effects did not differ by sex. Via ScienceDaily.
